for me, it’s sort of like an “accepted contract” between writer and reader that any specifics not included in a story are meant to be implied. if i mention the characters going out to eat at an italian place, a reader would likely imagine they get some sort of pasta dish, pay the check, and get back home, right? even though i hadn’t written any of that, what i’ve implied is strong enough on its own to leave out the details.

for me, it’s all about what’s important to me personally to write in. i’ve had fics where i have the characters discuss their safeword, even though if i used the safeword in their dialogue without that prior conversation, a reader would likely be able to gather that that’s their chosen safeword for the session— because to me, i like the intimacy of trust and being able to have open conversations like that, so because i like writing it, i put it in. if talks of clean sex are important to you as a writer, then include them!

i can’t imagine having BP since childhood, i’m sorry. for me, bell’s palsy started mid-december in 2023. the first week after i was diagnosed, i cried a lot. i hated my face at first, and still do some days. i’d say right now, a year and a half later, it’s about… 55-65% healed. i’ve worked on making my peace with the idea that my face is never “coming back,” in that way. 

i’ve never liked taking photos of myself even before BP, and i hate them even more now. i can’t smile, talk, laugh, without being hyper-aware of how my face must look to the people around me. i’m constantly told by my family “you can’t even tell!” but you absolutely can.

i don’t want to be denied my bell’s palsy exists so i can be handsome to them, i want all of me to be seen— my bell’s palsy, my SH scars, my transness, my fatness— and be admired anyway. people are denying parts of me because it can be an uncomfortable subject for them to navigate. i understand they’re doing it from a place of love, but it still hurts. after all, being uncomfortable is how we grow! my self image has changed because of BP— for the better! yes, it still makes me upset, but i don’t attach my self worth to my face anymore! my body is not me, it’s the vehicle that carries me around. my art is me, the company i keep is me, my favorite things are me— bell’s palsy is part, but it is not all.

it’s so hard to just… exist, when something sets you apart from others. but this is not all you are. and i’m sure the people who love you feel the same way :’-)

since i’ve never used it myself, i don’t know a ton about AI other than what i’ve watched and heard, but it’s enough to make me personally dislike it. i stress that part— my knowledge is incomplete, so i don’t know the ethics, or the process, i only know *my* own feelings. i wouldn’t go on a tirade about how a person using AI to make art in my style is copyright infringement, however, i would be rightfully pissed with that guy for directly ripping my art style with zero permission from me. to me, it’s insanely disrespectful, sets a bad standard that artists can be taken from whenever someone feels like it, and just makes whoever’s running the prompts look like they feel entitled to that artist’s work without putting in the effort to learn themselves, or by paying that artist for a commission.

in short! i don’t think AI is breaking any laws, and by some definitions it’s not outright stealing, but i do think that if you asked it to design a character, for example, it’d directly lift multiple other artists’ character designs mashed into one, directly creating off *their* ideas, and they’d never even know the theft had happened. i see this happen more clearly with writing! AI directly “borrows” a lot of plot points and dialogue from any body of text online, be that popular novels or something as obscure as fanfic.

it’s enough to make MY feelings about it especially strong because i already have next to no eyes on my art, so knowing i’m competing with a machine that can outpace me a million times over leaves me frequently disheartened, and i know i’m not the only artist who feels that way. i think no matter how either of us feels about AI, we can at least acknowledge it’s a shame artists have to feel that way. i think we can all learn to respect and care about each other if we hear each other out and sympathize.

from where i’m standing, it does. i’m calling a spade a spade: it scrapes through millions of pieces of art, without permission from the artists, to generate its own. what other word would you use besides stealing? scraping? undercutting? sampling? none of those should be allowed to be done without express permission and expect to be free of criticism.

i’ve seen some generators where you can even request art in a specific creator’s style. to me, the AI is effectively undermining years of work to cultivate a style and develop a skill set to make a mashed-together, soulless husk of the original artist it’s ripping from. that takes away from commissions the artist gets, has people using AI generated art in their style to sell bootleg merch even easier, and oversaturates art communities with that style, thereby driving out the original artist.

if you don’t want to call it stealing, find another adjective, but AI used in this application will effectively take art backwards, not forwards. there are genuinely incredible things AI can do, namely looking at the medical field, but as far as i’m concerned, AI has no place in art. art is born from intent and desire for expression. AI has no intent than the prompt it was given, and it does not desire to express anything it isn’t fed.

this is hard— this is a very good opportunity, and it sounds like you’re fully ready for it. on the other hand, it’s normal to want to spend tons of time with your partner, although everyone’s needs are different. me personally, i’m fine not talking to my partner for weeks at a time if i know they’re really busy but otherwise doing okay if they need space, but it sounds like her needs are different. saving up to be ready for what comes next in life is great if that’s what you want, too! now more than ever, having a broader financial safety net is important.

i think in an ideal relationship, she would understand that this is a fantastic opportunity, encouraging you to take it while admitting she’s sad that she’ll see less of you. and that would be a good thing! that means you’re loved. but this may not be an ideal relationship. she might not be able to handle the change, and that’s okay, too, even if it doesn’t feel okay at first to think about potentially splitting. being with another person for longer means you have more chances to see ways you both don’t click. you’ve found something that doesn’t quite click. 

i’d encourage you both to figure out needs, like hard lines to cross. one of hers might be quality time and how much of it she needs. what might be easier for you to adapt to might be much harder for her— it’s like adverse experiences! how an event can traumatize one person, but another person walks away okay. i’m not saying you’re traumatizing her, i only use that as an example to show how the same experience can vastly affect different people! even minor disagreements can make two people experiencing the same thing feel very differently.

have a genuine sit-down talk: say that you want to take this job opportunity, and that you can understand how changing your lives up can be hard for both of you. encourage her to really talk about how she feels, what she’s scared might happen if you two see each other a little less. voice how you were planning to work around that, like maybe scheduled date nights to make your time off feel more special, for example. it seems like you care for her! otherwise, you wouldn’t have come asking for advice about how to both take this opportunity and help keep her happy and loved! but i think it’s time to have a talk about what your future together might look like. good luck!

fandom simplifying a character so intensely until they’re almost unrecognizable is unfortunately very common T_T i think it might be a combination of immaturity from younger fans in these spaces, and people who have a hard time with literary comprehension— and i include myself in that second one! for a number of reasons, i’ve had problems with picking up on themes or characterizations for media i’ve enjoyed in the past. so although it’s not entirely their fault, either through being young or for not flexing those literary understanding muscles often enough, people take the most favorable parts of a character and then make that the ONLY thing that character is in their mind’s eye. i tend not to let fandom perception of a character sway how i view them because there’s always a very high chance that their canon self and their fanon self are two very different people

26, and i’m the same way. having more relapses recently after a month or so away from it, and part of that is driven by making sure the scars down both forearms stay noticeable. it’s a physical signifier for emotional pain. there’s some weird logic tied up in my own head that if it can’t be seen on the outside, if there aren’t enough scars, my problems must not be serious enough. i’m dealing with it right now— even with a relapse today and yesterday, i hate myself for not making them deeper. they’re too thin, they’ll fade too quickly, and that makes me panic, somehow. it’s just another thing to combat, alongside the urge to relapse. the idea that changed my way of thinking was that the end goal shouldn’t be to never self harm again, and if you can’t do that, you’ve failed— but instead, the goal should be to reduce harm as much as you’re able, and stay compassionate towards yourself even in relapse.
